lines.x: I'm used to being your assistant, so I bet I can take care of any work you throw at me. But don't you pile everything on me just because I said that!

It's so much easier working at Rhodes Island than the observation station. You have no idea how busy things get there! Not only do I have to pull all-nighters, but everyone's always coming to me for help. They even said they'd push for me to become a section director… You think I'll make a good director? Hehe, it's still too early for me to think about that.

Kjerag? I like the place. Everyone there takes really good care of me. When I was testing Originium samples with my local assistants, they all suddenly bowed their heads in unison. It kind of freaked me out, and it wasn't until later that I found out they were praying to Kjeragandr for me and the experiment.

My coworkers at Rhine Lab like to tell our new staff how I used to be, half-jokingly. Stuff like how I insisted on recording data even during a liquid Originium leak, but that 'just because something is dangerous doesn't mean it's important.' Gotta say, I'm actually pretty miffed about that. Whether it was actually important or not is something we'll have to wait for the future to find out.

Pramanix's a really good friend. I doubt I'll ever revere Kjeragandr as much as she does, or anyone from Kjerag, but I can feel just how crystal clear and resilient their minds are. For real, this is god's presence.

There was a researcher in Kjerag who told me he's afraid of new discoveries now, because of how they always shatter the framework of current science. I know not everyone who believes in science looks forward to its changes, but me? I always love seeing the new possibilities.

Not long ago, my parents sent my sister a long letter and a whole bunch of goodies from our hometown, meant for me. I may not have made up my mind yet, but… Doctor, do you have any gift ideas for old-fashioned types?

Hm… Oh, hey, Doctor. This is an astrological star chart I got from Sia. I wanted to make some adjustments based on the observation data I got at Kjerag… Since when have I been interested in astrology, you ask? This too, is a field that those who walked before us explored. It may be riddled with errors, but that doesn't mean it's completely devoid of value.

In Kjerag, I witnessed a power that I couldn't comprehend for the first time. The further I walk down this path of science, the more I am pushing the boundaries of the unknown... Don't worry. I respect all explanations for the unknown, and I know I will one day demystify it.
Huh? Is the Doctor asleep? Then I guess I'll take the chance to get a nap in, too.

It's great to see you again, Doctor. I reviewed my time onboard and my workflow at Rhodes Island. I'm pretty confident I can handle anything that comes my way. Hm? You've always been satisfied with my work? Hehe…
There's still room for improvement. Looks like I will have plenty to do once I get back.
Huh, still the same medals as before. So pretty.
Nothing exists independently of us. Rather, we observe and change everything. That's why I believe in science.
Long time no see, everybody. Time to work together again.
'Switching firing position!'… Got everything memorized. We'll be fine.
Don't worry. I know our departure time.
In position to engage the enemy. Ready your weapons.
Yep, I'm here.
Same tactics as before?
In position.
I'll do my best!
I convey my starlight to the darkness.
I have charge of this sector.
I will stop you.
There is no limit to the power that mankind may realize.
Incredible commanding, Doctor! Hm? My performance is incredible, too? That's giving me too much credit. I came prepared, that's all.
A victory meeting expectations after careful planning. Now we can all relax.
Huh? This variable…
Oh, don't worry. Once we identify the source of the problem, we'll get this taken care of, easy.
Let me set my alarm.
Whoa?!
Don't let anybody know I'm slacking off—wait, you didn't know? Drat...
Arknights.

Hello Doctor. The lab's too suffocating, so I came out here for a little fresh air. Are you here for a break, too? Hm? Happy New Year? Wait, is it past midnight already?! I was gonna head out with Sia and get some snacks… Oh well, it can wait. Happy New Year, Doctor!
Hey, Doctor. Do you have time to come to the lab and check out my latest breakthrough?

Happy Birthday! I have a present for you—a planetarium I made myself, by hand! When I was a kid, my parents wouldn't let me make them, and it took me so much work just to fix one myself. Come, switch off the lamp and check this out. It even lights up! You think it's a little cliché? Come on, Doctor. Don't say that, even as a joke.

Anything that mankind can gain from these stacks of paper pales in comparison to the reality offered by planting your feet on the ground or gazing up at the stars. I look forward to witnessing more miracles in the mists of the unknown… both at Rhine Lab… and at Rhodes Island.
